requirement:
An outline selector MUST be a `/`-separated path of segments from the file's
root node to an outline node; the empty selector MUST select the root node. A
named node's segment MUST be `kind[name]`. An anonymous node's segment MUST be
`kind@hash`, where `hash` is the first twelve hexadecimal digits of its identity
hash under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`. Siblings whose
segments would otherwise be identical MUST be disambiguated by `#N`, their
one-based position among those siblings in source order, except `line` nodes:
identical lines are interchangeable, so a `line` selector MUST resolve when any
line with that content exists in the file. In names, `%`, `[`, `]`, `/`, `#`,
`@`, and whitespace MUST be percent-encoded as UTF-8 bytes, so selectors are
reversible. Line numbers MUST NOT form part of a selector.
rationale:
**Judgment: the requirement is met.** The implementation covers every obligation, and the tests cover the main points of the design space. I did not run the tests; I judged them from their source.

**Implementation**
- **Selector shape.** `OutlineNode` in `src/outline/mod.rs` has a root with an empty `segment` and `selector` (`root_node`). Every other node has a segment, and `disambiguate` builds the full selector as the `/`-joined path of segments from the root. No line numbers appear in selectors.
- **Named and anonymous segments.**
  - `Segment::base` in `src/outline/selector.rs` emits `kind[name]` for named nodes and `kind@hash` for anonymous ones.
  - `Builder::finish` and `plain_text` take the hash from `identity_hash[..HASH_DIGITS]`, and `HASH_DIGITS` is 12.
  - The label uses the identity hash, not the structural hash, as the structural_hash requirement specifies. How that hash is computed is that requirement's concern.
- **Percent-encoding.**
  - `encode_name` encodes `%`, `[`, `]`, `/`, `#`, `@` and any Unicode whitespace as UTF-8 bytes.
  - `decode_name` reverses this. It rejects malformed escapes, raw delimiters, raw whitespace and escapes that are not UTF-8.
  - Multi-part names, such as a trait impl's `impl[Thing/Trait]`, encode each part separately and join the parts with `/`. That joining is defined by the Rust-specific selector requirements, not by this one.
- **Disambiguation.** `disambiguate` groups siblings by identical base segment, in source order, and appends a one-based `#N` to each member of a group with more than one. It skips `line` nodes, as required.
- **Resolution.**
  - `Outline::resolve` parses the selector and walks it from the root. The empty selector gives the root.
  - A `line` segment matches the first line with that content, so it resolves whenever any such line exists.
  - `parse_selector`, `split_segments` and `parse_segment` reject malformed input: bad kind, unclosed or nested brackets, wrong hash length, `#0`, trailing text and empty segments.
  - `ParsedSource::resolve` in `src/inputs.rs` reports invalid, ambiguous and not-found selectors with distinct messages.
- **Markers.** All of this code carries `{impl}` markers for the requirement. I found no selector-producing code without one. The other places that use `.selector` only consume the selectors it produces.

**Tests**
- `names_round_trip_through_percent_encoding` checks the exact encoding of all special characters, tab and non-ASCII text, plus the round trip. It also checks rejection of raw `/`, a malformed `%zz` escape and raw whitespace.
- `parses_named_anonymous_and_ordinal_segments` checks the empty selector, a multi-part name, `#N`, hash lowercasing and seven invalid forms.
- `rust_selectors_follow_syntactic_ancestry` checks that every generated selector resolves back to its own node. It covers duplicate names with `#1`/`#2` and a name that needs percent-encoding. It also checks that the empty selector gives the root, that an ambiguous selector fails and that a missing one fails.
- `anonymous_selectors_use_identity_hashes` checks that an anonymous segment has 12 hex digits and that selectors survive an inserted sibling. It checks that editing a node's own text invalidates its selector, and that duplicate anonymous nodes get `#1`/`#2`.
- `plain_text_lines_are_interchangeable_anonymous_nodes` checks that identical lines share one selector with no `#N`, and that it resolves. It also checks that whitespace-only differences share a selector while `two words` and `twowords` differ.

**Gaps:** none found, and no FIXME comments.

text: :::{req} outline_selectors
An outline selector MUST be a `/`-separated path of segments from the file's
root node to an outline node; the empty selector MUST select the root node. A
named node's segment MUST be `kind[name]`. An anonymous node's segment MUST be
`kind@hash`, where `hash` is the first twelve hexadecimal digits of its identity
hash under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`. Siblings whose
segments would otherwise be identical MUST be disambiguated by `#N`, their
one-based position among those siblings in source order, except `line` nodes:
identical lines are interchangeable, so a `line` selector MUST resolve when any
line with that content exists in the file. In names, `%`, `[`, `]`, `/`, `#`,
`@`, and whitespace MUST be percent-encoded as UTF-8 bytes, so selectors are
reversible. Line numbers MUST NOT form part of a selector.
:::{req} structural_hash
A node's structural hash MUST be the SHA-256 digest of an unambiguous encoding of
its outline-relevant structure, including siblings its profile attaches to it:
the kinds of its named grammar nodes and, in source order, its text pieces. A
text piece MUST be the text of a leaf token, or text inside a node that no child
token covers. Each text piece MUST be hashed as its ordered list of words, where
words are separated by whitespace, the whitespace itself, including leading and
trailing whitespace, is never hashed, and each word is encoded separately, so
`ab cd` and `abcd` differ. The same rule MUST apply in every language. Comments
MUST be excluded, except comment kinds the profile includes; the Rust profile
MUST include doc comments. For an included comment, only its text MUST be hashed,
not its delimiter tokens such as `//`, `///`, `//!`, `/*`, `*/`, or a leading `*`,
so reflowing it across more or fewer lines does not change the hash. A `line`
node's hash MUST be computed by the same word rule over the line's text. A node's
identity hash MUST be computed the same way but MUST also exclude its outline
descendants and their attached siblings, so editing a descendant does not change
its ancestors' selectors.
